title_tag: 10 Best Beach Resorts in Dubai (2026): Prices Compared
meta_description: Dubai beach resorts from €148 to €967 a night compared on private beach, pools, kids' clubs and breakfast, from Jumeirah and JBR to Bluewaters and the Palm.
h1_main: 10 Best Beach Resorts in Dubai in 2026
author_role: 10 Dubai beach resorts compared on nightly price, guest score, beach, pools, kids' club and breakfast
lead: For most couples the Dubai beach resort to book is Banyan Tree on Bluewaters at €570 a night, with breakfast, a 500 m private beach and the joint-top guest score of the ten (9.5). The best value on the sand is Sheraton JBR at €231 with breakfast, families should look at Le Meridien Mina Seyahi (€275, kids' club and free waterpark), and the splurge is Four Seasons Jumeirah at €868 for 70 m² rooms.

The catch most visitors miss: plenty of "beach hotels" in Dubai only run a shuttle to the sand. Nine of the 10 here sit on their own beach, from Jumeirah and JBR to Bluewaters and the Creek; the tenth, Mileo on the Palm, gives free access to a private beach 200 m away. They were compared on price for the same night, guest score, beach type, pools, kids' club, breakfast and room size. Filter by breakfast, luxury, families, couples or budget below, or jump to the comparison table.
price_note: Lowest nightly rate for 2 adults on 13–14 January 2027. Dates, room type and board change it; taxes and the Dubai tourism fee are added at booking.

items.title: Banyan Tree Dubai at Bluewaters

pills.label: In 15:00, out 12:00
pills.body: Check-in from 15:00, check-out until 12:00. Photo ID and a credit card are asked for at check-in, and the resort wants your arrival time in advance.

pills.body: Children of any age are welcome, but from 7 years they are charged as adults; extra beds for 7+ are free. No kids' club is listed. Wheelchair accessible, with an emergency cord in the bathroom.

pills.body: The signature Banyan Tree Spa with sauna and steam room, plus a heated outdoor pool with a shallow end set in gardens.

pills.label: Island resort
pills.body: Asian-styled rooms in natural materials, lush gardens and an island position across the bridge from JBR. Guests score comfort 9.7 and location 9.6, among the top marks here.

items.skip: if you travel with children over 6: they pay adult rates and no kids' club is listed, so Le Meridien (#4) or Four Seasons (#3) suit families better.

review: Banyan Tree is the resort we would book first for a beach trip to Dubai. €570 a night buys the joint-highest guest score on the page (9.5, level with Mileo), a 54 m² Bliss room with a balcony and bath, and breakfast, on a rate with free cancellation and nothing to pay until you arrive.

The beach is the reason to pick it: 500 metres of private sand on Bluewaters Island, with Ain Dubai as the backdrop and JBR and the Marina a short hop over the bridge. Next to it you get a heated outdoor pool, the Banyan Tree Spa and three listed restaurants, including Demon Duck by Alvin Leung.

Compared with Four Seasons (#3) it costs €298 less and includes breakfast, though its rooms are smaller (54 m² against 70 m²). Compared with Address Beach Resort (#6) it gives you an island beach across the bridge instead of The Walk at JBR on your doorstep.

The catch is for families: children from 7 years pay as adults, and no kids' club is listed. On top of the nightly price come a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night.

review: The Sheraton is the cheapest way on this page to wake up on a private beach with breakfast paid for. €231 a night gets a Deluxe Room with JBR view, private beach access and breakfast, on a rate you can cancel for free and pay at the hotel.

You get newly renovated rooms and lobby, one large outdoor pool with a pool bar, squash courts, a spa and five places to eat, from Seafield's Mediterranean menu to Peacock's Chinese dinners. The Walk at JBR is a few steps away.

Against Al Habtoor Grand (#8), it costs €40 more but includes breakfast (Habtoor's standard breakfast rate is €245 and non-refundable) and scores higher (8.8 against 8.3). Against the JBR hotels in our JBR hotel comparison, it is one of the few with its own stretch of sand.

The catches: the cheapest room is 36 m², the hotel takes an AED 1,000 cash deposit at check-in (refunded at check-out), and a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night are added.

review: Four Seasons is the splurge pick for a beach holiday that still keeps the city close. €868 a night gets a 70 m² Deluxe City View Room, the largest entry room on the page, with a balcony, soaking tub, rain shower and a TV built into the mirror, and the rate has free cancellation with no prepayment.

Outside the room you get a private beach with cabanas and day villas, two outdoor pools plus an indoor one, tennis and padel courts, a spa, and Mercury Rooftop facing Burj Khalifa. Guests rate cleanliness, comfort and staff 9.7, among the best marks of all ten.

It is also the best family alternative to Le Meridien (#4) if budget allows: special programmes for younger guests and free extra beds for anyone 3–17. Compared with Banyan Tree (#1), you pay €298 more for 16 m² more room and three pools, but lose the included breakfast.
The catch: the cheapest room looks at the city, and breakfast is not part of that rate. Taxes and charges are added at booking.

review: Le Meridien Mina Seyahi is the family resort on this list. €275 a night with breakfast buys a room with unlimited Jungle Bay waterpark access, a kids' club with two kids' pools, and the longest beach on the page at 1,200 metres.

You also get four pools (one rooftop, one infinity), a water sports centre, the Club Mina gym and Barasti, the beach bar with live entertainment. Board is flexible: breakfast and dinner costs €344 and all-inclusive €458 for two, both with free cancellation.

Compared with Jumeirah Mina Al Salam (#5), which also gives free waterpark access (Wild Wadi) and a kids' club at a sister hotel, it costs €692 less a night. Compared with the Sheraton (#2), it is €44 more but adds the kids' club and the waterpark. If you want the waterpark without the hotel, see our Dubai water parks comparison.

The catches: the cheapest room is 32 m² and faces the skyline, the guest score (8.5) is the second-lowest of the ten, and a 10.5% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night are added on top.

review: Mina Al Salam is the pick if you want the classic Madinat Jumeirah stay: Arabian-style buildings on the waterways and two kilometres of private beach. €967 a night covers a 50 m² Deluxe Ocean Room with a sea-view terrace, breakfast and unlimited Wild Wadi Waterpark access.

Families get more than the price suggests: cots and extra beds are free up to 11, the resort description lists Jumeirah Circle (the supervised kids' club at sister hotel Al Qasr) and family pools, and three-night stays add a day at Dubai Parks and Resorts.

Against Four Seasons (#3) you pay €99 more but get breakfast and waterpark access included, with a smaller room (50 m² against 70 m²). Against Le Meridien (#4), the waterpark and kids' club deal is similar, for €692 more a night, so this is a setting choice, not a value choice.

Its booking terms are generous: free cancellation until 23 December 2026 and nothing to pay until arrival. Added on top: a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night.

review: Address Beach Resort sells the view as much as the beach. Its infinity pool, about 294 metres up, holds the record as the world's highest outdoor infinity pool, looking over Bluewaters, Ain Dubai, the Palm and the Marina. The beachfront and The Walk at JBR are downstairs.

€474 a night was a limited-time deal rate on our date, and it is a strong package: daily breakfast, one floating breakfast per stay, infinity pool access, and check-in and check-out at 14:00, with free cancellation. There are nine restaurants, including Mott 32 and ZETA Seventy Seven, and a spa on the 75th floor.

Compared with Nikki Beach (#7), it costs €40 more and swaps a beach club for a tower resort with far more dining. Compared with the Sheraton (#2) along the same beach, you pay double for the pool, views and a 9.4 score.
Families should note the sky pool turns 16+ after 11:30; children have a splash pad and kids' pool instead. Taxes and charges come on top of €474.

review: Nikki Beach is the resort for people who want the beach club, not just the beach. €434 a night buys a 55 m² Covet Room with balcony and breakfast, on Pearl Jumeira island with 450 metres of private sand and free entry to the Nikki Beach Club.

Rooms are made for longer days in: a MyBar, surround sound with the house playlist and walk-in closets. Beyond the beach you get outdoor pools, five dining venues, a spa with ice baths and IV drips, a free gym and a Kids' Playroom.

It sits on the Jumeirah coast like Four Seasons (#3) but costs half as much and includes breakfast; the difference is the beach club against three pools and kids' programmes, and room size (55 m² against 70 m²). It is also one of the closest resorts here to Dubai International, about 15 minutes away.

The terms are friendly: free cancellation until 14:00 on the arrival day and payment at the hotel. Added on top: a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night.

review: Al Habtoor Grand is the cheapest 5★ resort on this page that sits on the open Gulf beach. €191 a night (a deal rate on our date, 30% off) gets a 40 m² Tower room with partial sea view, private beach access and discounts of 20% on food and drink and 30% at the spa.

For children it has the most to do on the list after Le Meridien: three pools including an infinity pool, adult and kids' water slides and a splash area. Adults get 13 restaurants and bars, from O Beach to The Underground Pub.

Compared with the Sheraton (#2) a few minutes along JBR, the room is bigger (40 m² against 36 m²) and €40 cheaper, but breakfast is extra and the guest score is lower (8.3 against 8.8). Compared with Le Meridien (#4), you lose the kids' club and the waterpark, and save €84.

Check the terms: the standard breakfast-included rate (€245) and the €230 room-only rate are non-refundable and paid before arrival. Added on top: a 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and the AED 20 tourism fee per night.

guide.h2: Which Dubai Beach Resort Should You Book?
guide.html:
• Best all-round, couples: #1 Banyan Tree Bluewaters, €570. Joint-top score (9.5), 500 m private beach, breakfast included.
  • Cheapest real beach resort with breakfast: #2 Sheraton JBR, €231, private beach steps from The Walk.
  • Families: #4 Le Meridien Mina Seyahi, €275 for the kids' club, two kids' pools and free Jungle Bay waterpark. Bigger budget: #3 Four Seasons, €868 (free extra beds to 17) or #5 Mina Al Salam, €967 (Wild Wadi included).
  • Splurge: #3 Four Seasons, €868, for 70 m² rooms, three pools and staff, comfort and cleanliness scores of 9.7.
  • Views and a beach club: #6 Address Beach Resort, €474, with the world's highest infinity pool, or #7 Nikki Beach, €434 with the Nikki Beach Club on site.
  • Tight budget: #8 Al Habtoor Grand, €191 on JBR beach, #9 Mileo, €165 on the Palm (beach 200 m away) or #10 Vida Creek Beach, €148 near the airport.

Want more hotels in one area? Compare JBR hotels, Dubai Marina hotels and Palm Jumeirah hotels. For kids' clubs across the city, see the best family resorts in Dubai, and for the top end, the best luxury hotels in Dubai.

guide.h2: Staying on the Beach in Dubai: Areas, Getting Around and Extra Costs
guide.html:
Which beach to stay on

  • Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim (Four Seasons, Nikki Beach, Mina Al Salam): closest to Downtown and Dubai International; Four Seasons is 15 minutes' drive from Burj Khalifa, Nikki Beach 15 minutes from the airport. Mina Al Salam shares Madinat Jumeirah's 2 km beach.
  • Al Sufouh and Mina Seyahi (Le Meridien): the long family beach with Jungle Bay waterpark and Barasti; Mall of the Emirates is 8 km.
  • Bluewaters (Banyan Tree): an island beach under Ain Dubai, across the bridge from JBR.
  • JBR (Sheraton, Address, Al Habtoor Grand): beach plus The Walk's restaurants and shops outside the door.
  • Palm Jumeirah (Mileo): the budget way onto the Palm, with free private beach access 200 m from the hotel.
  • Dubai Creek Harbour (Vida Creek Beach): a creek beach 10 km from Dubai International, best for short stays.

Getting around

The JBR, Bluewaters and Palm resorts list Al Maktoum International as the nearest airport (21–30 km), but most flights land at Dubai International: Vida Creek Beach is 10 km away, Nikki Beach about 15 minutes, Four Seasons about 20 km and Le Meridien 31 km. Parking is free at all ten, and Mina Al Salam runs shuttles to Mall of the Emirates and Souk Madinat Jumeirah.

What costs extra

  • Taxes and fees: the nightly prices shown exclude them. Where the rates break them down, a 10% service charge (10.5% at Le Meridien), 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and a Dubai tourism fee of AED 20 per room per night are added on top.
  • Breakfast: included at six of the ten; €33 at Le Meridien (room-only rates) and Al Habtoor Grand; not shown for Four Seasons, Mileo and Vida Creek Beach.
  • Extra beds: free at Four Seasons (ages 3–17), Mina Al Salam (to 11), Banyan Tree (7+, who pay adult rates) and Nikki Beach (4–5); AED 125–400 a night elsewhere, with Address the highest.
  • Deposits: the Sheraton collects AED 1,000 in cash on arrival, refunded at check-out.

On the water

The rates here are for mid-January, the cooler winter season. Most of these beaches are a short ride from the marinas: compare jet ski tours, scuba diving in Dubai and dinner cruises if you want to see the coast from the sea.

faqs.q: What is the best beach resort in Dubai?
faqs.a: Banyan Tree Dubai at Bluewaters, from €570 a night with breakfast. It shares the highest guest score of the ten compared (9.5, with Mileo), a 500 m private beach and a 54 m² entry room. For more space and three pools, Four Seasons Resort at Jumeirah Beach (€868) is the step up.

faqs.q: How much does a beach resort in Dubai cost per night?
faqs.a: On a January weeknight for two adults, the ten resorts here ran from €148 (Vida Creek Beach, a 4★ on the creek) to €967 (Jumeirah Mina Al Salam, with breakfast). The median was about €355. A 10% service charge, 5% VAT, a 7% municipality fee and an AED 20 tourism fee per night come on top.

faqs.q: Which Dubai beach resort is best for families?
faqs.a: Le Meridien Mina Seyahi at €275 with breakfast: it has a kids' club with two kids' pools, a 1,200 m beach and free unlimited Jungle Bay waterpark access. With a bigger budget, Four Seasons gives free extra beds up to 17, and Mina Al Salam includes Wild Wadi and the Jumeirah Circle kids' club at its sister hotel. See also our family resorts comparison.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest Dubai hotel with a private beach?
faqs.a: Vida Creek Beach Hotel at €148, but its beach faces Dubai Creek. On the Gulf, Al Habtoor Grand on JBR starts at €191 (a deal rate, breakfast not listed) and the Sheraton Jumeirah Beach Resort at €231 includes breakfast.

faqs.q: Do Dubai beach resorts include breakfast?
faqs.a: Six of the ten here include breakfast in the cheapest rate: Banyan Tree, Sheraton, Le Meridien, Mina Al Salam, Address Beach Resort and Nikki Beach. At Al Habtoor Grand it is listed at €33 on the standard rate; Four Seasons, Mileo and Vida Creek Beach did not show breakfast on their lowest rate.

faqs.q: Which area of Dubai has the best beach resorts: Jumeirah, JBR or the Palm?
faqs.a: Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim (Four Seasons, Nikki Beach, Mina Al Salam) are closest to Downtown and the main airport. JBR (Sheraton, Address, Al Habtoor Grand) puts The Walk outside the door. Bluewaters (Banyan Tree) is an island beach next to JBR, and the Palm is covered in our Palm Jumeirah hotels comparison.

faqs.q: Can children use the infinity pool at Address Beach Resort?
faqs.a: Yes, but only until 11:30. From 11:30 the infinity pool and its dining area are for guests aged 16 and over, every day. Younger children have a kids' pool and the Kids Splash Pad.

methodology: We compared beachfront resorts across Dubai's coast (Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim, Al Sufouh, Bluewaters, JBR, the Palm and the Creek) on live prices for the same night, two adults and one night in mid-January, and kept 10 from €148 to €967: nine on their own beach and one (Mileo on the Palm) with free private beach access 200 m away. Each was scored on the nightly price, guest score, beach type and length, pools, kids' club, what the cheapest rate includes (breakfast, waterpark access, cancellation), the size of the entry room, child policies and distances to the airport and city. Rankings reward the best all-round beach stay first, then the clearest pick for each type of traveller.
